 : Judgment :

The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/102/2012-13 dated 06.08.2021 in respect of Sy. No.3/1B measuring 328 Sq.
feet of Venkatala village, Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.

.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property bearing Sy. No. 3/1B measuring 328 Sq.
feet A.P. No.125/2022 situated at Venkatala village, Yelahanka Hobli has been acquired under Gazette notification No. S.O. No.1622 (E) dated 02.07.2010.

Prior to that, Preliminary Notification issued under S.O. No.3159(E) dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification issued under S.O.
No.1622(E) dated 02.07.2010.
Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO has awarded a total sum of Rs. 4,30,992/- as compensation for 328 Sq. feet of the land belongs to the petitioner.
The petitioner received the same under protest and filed an application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs. 10,000/- per Sq. feet as on 26.06.2012.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No.3 for consideration.
.3. In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contention urged by the petitioner are baseless and the same are made without any substance.
The petitioner has not produced any relevant documents to justify his claim for enhancement of compensation and the claim of the A.P. No.125/2022 petitioner cannot be sustained in law.
Hence, question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the claim of the petitioner is liable to be dismissed by the respondent No.3.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.

.4. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 102 104/ 2012-13 dated 06.08.2021.
.5.
Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :

sentences.text: The petitioner claims that the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 is wholly erroneous, contrary to law, materials on record and in violation of principles of natural justice.

The petitioner claims that the respondent No.3 committed a legal misconduct in not following the documents filed by the petitioner for A.P.
No.125/2022 deciding the market value.
The Arbitrator failed to appreciate the fact that the respondent No.1 and 2 have not produced any documents to justify the award passed by him.
The petitioner further claims that the award dated 24.05.2011 passed by the respondent No. 2 is not in accordance with the guidelines under Section 3G(7) of NH Act.
The Arbitrator has failed to appreciate the claim of the petitioner and passed inappropriate order.
The Arbitrator has failed to appreciate that the respondent no.2 has not produced any document to justify his award.
The award amount is not at all matching with the market value for the prime land of the petitioner.

The lands nearer to the corporation/town municipalities for commercial use limits or within the corporation/town municipalities limits are more valuable that the lands situated outside and the acquired land could be used in the vicinity acquires a special value.

The respondent No. 3 enhanced just and meager compensation without taken into consideration material evidence placed A.P.
No.125/2022 before the Court, which is against probabilities of the case.

Accordingly,
prayed for reconsidering the impugned award and also alternative prayer to remand the matter to the Arbitrator for fresh consideration.

.6. The respondent No.1 and 2 filed a detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the respondent No. 3 passed the award as per the guidance value produced before the Arbitrator pertaining to the year 2011.
The petitioner is attempting to mislead this Court by drawing reference to incorrect/wholly inapplicable guidance notification.
The respondent No.1 and 2 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioner in the petition.

The Arbitrator/ respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner by considering the material evidence on record for enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under the LA Act in A.P. No.125/2022 accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
.7. The petitioner along with the petition filed I.A. No. 1 under Section 34(3) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, for condonation of delay if any filing the petition.

.8. The above application is supported with the affidavit of petitioner, wherein, it is stated that the order has not been communicated to him and when he approached the concerned authority on 18.04.2022, he came to know about the order and he immediately applied for copy of the order and he got the same on 26.05.2022.

Thereafter, filed this petition and accordingly prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.
.9.
The respondent No.1 has not filed any objections to the IA.

On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the petition filed by the petitioner is within time ?
2) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
3) What order or award?

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative Point No.2 : In the negative Point No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .13. POINT NO.1: Perused the I.A. No.1 along with affidavit that has been filed for condonation of delay in filing the petition, satisfied with reasons therein and the said application is not opposed by the respondent No. 1.
Accordingly, I am of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to condone the delay in filing the petition.
Accordingly the point No. 1 is answered in the affirmative.
.14. POINT No.2:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The petitioner Sri. P. Alikutti is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.3/1B measuring to an extent of 328 Sq. feet of Venkatala village, Yelahanka, Bengaluru North Additional Taluka and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010, that has been published in the official Gazette on 02.07.2010,
is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2/Special Land Acquisition and Alikutti P vs The Project Director And General ... on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58239655/

sentences.text: Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs. 1,314/- per Sq. feet for the A.P. No.125/2022 acquired land.
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.4,30,992/-
being the land value
was disbursed to the petitioner as compensation

Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the petitioner Sri. P. Alikutti filed an application before the respondent No.3 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs. 10,000/- per Sq. feet as on 15.06.2012.
On basis of the said application, the respondent No.3 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /CR / 102 / 104/2012-13 dated 06.08.2021.
The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.2,625/- per Sq. feet from Rs. 1,314/- per Sq. feet and awarded additional compensation of Rs. 1,311/- per Sq. feet.
.16. The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 without considering the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner and also without considering the claim of the petitioner that A.P. No.125/2022 market value of the other properties have enhanced which is much higher than the compensation enhanced by the respondent No. 3.
The said claim of the petitioner is also found in first paragraph of the order / award at page No.3 wherein the Arbitrator / respondent No. 3 stated about claim of petitioner for enhancement.

On close perusal of the order passed by the respondent No. 3, it is clear that the respondent No. 3 considering the guidance value of the year 2011-12 published vide notification bearing No. CVC 19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 enhanced the compensation.

In the entire Lower Court Records, no where discloses that the petitioner has produced any documents to show that the market value of the acquired property is more than the compensation awarded by the respondent No. 3.
It is true that the petitioner has produced various citations before the Court, but there is no material on record to show that the award passed by the respondent No. 3 is patently illegal.
It is true that the petitioner has produced the award passed by the Arbitrator namely M.K. A.P. No.125/2022 Jagadish in LAQ/ARB/ANH/07/CR/01-2019-20 dated 09.01.2020.

As per the said order, the market value of the non agricultural land has been fixed at Rs. 5,781/-
per Sq. feet, but the said property is situated in Sy.No. 2/2 of Byatarayanapura village, but the property involved in this case is the property bearing Sy.No. 3/1B of Venkatala village.
Hence, the said order cannot considered by the Court to set aside the order of LAO.

Mere production of citation,
certainly will not come to the aid of petitioner unless and until the petitioner shows that the order is patently illegal or the Arbitrator has failed to consider the documents produced by the petitioner for enhancement of compensation.

In the case on hand, there is no material on record to show that the petitioner has produced any material before the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 to show that he has produced necessary documents which discloses that the market value of the acquired property is much more higher than the compensation enhanced by the Arbitrator.
All these facts are considered and discussed by the Arbitrator / A.P. No.125/2022 respondent No. 3 in the impugned order.

Accordingly, the point No.2 is answered in the negative.
.17. Point No.3: In view of my above findings, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER IA filed by the petitioner to condone the delay in filing the petition is allowed.
Petition filed under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by the petitioner is hereby dismissed.
